question: Is a store's own country the country of the business behind it, held on a business-entity record (the legal entity, its country and address) so a store can later trade through more than one, rather than a single field of the store?
alternatives: (a) A country field and the store's address, set by the seller: all five (a commonality, no difference: S02-VP-01|a country field, S02-VP-01|the store's address). (b) A business entity holds it, a legal entity with its own address, assignable to markets: Shopify (vendor choice; stated, observed, shipped: S02-VP-01|a business entity; S02-V-001, S02-V-009). (c) The billing address the merchant pays the platform from: Shopify (vendor choice; official page, stated, observed: S02-VP-01|the billing address; S02-V-003). (d) A location set on a map or by hand: Salla, Zid, Shopify, WooCommerce (vendor choice; stated, shipped, observed: S02-VP-01|the store's location). (e) The store's currency beside its address: Shopify (vendor choice; stated: S02-VP-01|the store's currency; S02-V-010). (f) A seat setting beside the country: Salla (vendor choice; stated: S02-VP-01|مقر المتجر; S02-V-014). (g) A country per storefront, shown as the store's: BigCommerce (vendor choice; stated: S02-VP-85|a market the store sells into; S02-V-871). Each platform carries its variants at once (coexistence A, c/RD1/points.tsv)
recommendation: Engineering's: (b) in its general form. The store's country is the country of a business-entity record; one entity per store at launch, the model allowing more, each assignable to markets as Shopify's are (S02-V-649; S02-VP-63 kept open). The address, a map location, the billing address and the currency are records of their own and never fill the country; a market may show buyers another country or address only as a display value (S02-D6). A seat, where the store is based (Salla's مقر المتجر, S02-SA-177), is held as the business record's address, not as a setting of its own beside the country. Rule: generality (PLAN.md section 6, step 4): one entity per store is the restricted form, reached by configuration; hide what is likely to change (section 1): every rule keyed on the seller's country reads one record (S02-E2)
trade_off: One more record per store at launch, and a term sellers may meet; in return a second legal entity, a move of country, or a market served through another entity needs no re-keying of the rules that depend on the seller's country
closes: Filling the country from the billing address, a map location, the currency or a seat setting, and a legal country per market apart from an entity: an engineering cost greater than the option's value, since two sources of one fact can disagree; a confirmed fact that Shopify itself holds the store address and the billing address to an entity's country (S02-V-066, S02-V-067)
cost_later: a redesign: with the country a field of the store, a second entity later re-keys every rule keyed on the seller's country (S02-VP-08 to S02-VP-19) and the records made under it. With the entity in place, a second one is a setting, which holds because S02-E2 has each order record the business that served it; without that record a second entity is a redesign of orders

question: When a seller moves country, does the store take on a new business record for the new country, keeping its catalogue, customers and orders, rather than changing its country in place?
alternatives: (a) Changed in place at any time: BigCommerce's default country (stated: S02-V-091, S02-BC-251), and WooCommerce's store country, whose change saved on a test store with orders and tax rates present, both reading back as before (observed: S02-V-087; S02-WC-523, S02-WC-525, S02-WC-526) (vendor choice: S02-VP-07|at any time). (b) Changed in place once conditions hold: every financial service deactivated, the store address in the entity's country, the billing address's country that of an active entity, one individual entity per person and country: Shopify (vendor choice; stated, observed: S02-VP-07|all financial services deactivated, S02-VP-07|the store address in the business entity's country, S02-VP-07|the billing address's country that of an active business entity, S02-VP-07|the person not already associated with an individual business entity in the country; S02-V-065, S02-V-066, S02-V-067, S02-V-069). (c) No one changes it; a change makes a new entity or account: Shopify for individual entities, WooPayments for its account (vendor choice; stated: S02-VP-06|no one; S02-V-268, S02-V-086). (d) The platform changes it: Shopify's support on request, for stores under its Plus contract and stores using several entities' payment accounts (stated: S02-V-064, S02-V-269); WooCommerce's code migrating a stored location's state code (shipped: S02-V-276) (vendor choice: S02-VP-06|the platform). The seller changes it in the admin on all five (a commonality: S02-VP-06|the seller)
recommendation: Engineering's: (c), with (d) for Sharrwah's staff where a contract or several entities bind it. A business entity's country never changes in place: a seller who moves adds an entity for the new country, which becomes the store's default, and the old one closes once nothing open rests on it. The conditions in (b), and those other subjects set (payment accounts, S-04; a new verification, S-07; tax forms, S-05), run as checks before the switch, each owner's check behind one interface. A display default country stays changeable at any time (S02-D6). Rule: hide what is likely to change (PLAN.md section 1), on what the references show: a lock while money is attached (S02-SH-250: every financial service off before a store's country changes), and a fixed country for an individual's entity (S02-SH-596) and for a payment account (S02-WC-182)
trade_off: A move takes a few steps (a new entity and its checks) instead of one edit; in return the contracts, provider accounts, tax forms and invoices made under the old country keep their meaning
closes: (a) for the legal country: an engineering cost greater than the option's value, since rules and records keyed on the country would change meaning silently. The confirmed facts are narrower: Shopify fixes an individual's entity's country (S02-SH-596) and changes a store's only once its financial services are off (S02-SH-250), and WooPayments fixes its account's country (S02-WC-182). WooCommerce's store country changes in place (S02-V-087), a store setting with no payment account bound to it: a reading, since WooPayments' own country stays fixed. (a) stays for a display default country, under S02-D6
cost_later: one module: with S02-D1's entity record, switching between 'add and switch' and 'edit in place' changes only the move's procedure; a redesign without the entity record, where records keep no country of their own

question: May each market sell in its own currency at its own prices, converted by Sharrwah at an exchange rate held for that market or set by the seller, every order keeping its amounts in both the market's currency and the store's? Three parts, each answered on its own: the two amounts on every record; where the rate is held; which markets carry their own currency
alternatives: (a) A currency per market: Salla, Zid, Shopify, and BigCommerce per storefront (business model; stated, observed, shipped: S02-VP-41|a market the store sells into; S02-V-676, S02-V-751, S02-V-600, S02-V-809); WooCommerce allows one base currency per store (S02-WC-085). (b) Prices per market: Salla, Zid, Shopify, BigCommerce (business model: S02-VP-49|a market the store sells into; S02-V-620). (c) Prices converted by the platform at the exchange rate where the seller chooses: Salla, Zid, WooCommerce (vendor choice; observed, stated: S02-VP-50|the platform; S02-V-690, S02-V-768, S02-V-908); Shopify isn't stated under that key, though its dynamic conversion (S02-SH-179, under S02-VP-42) reads the same, a reading. (d) A price by the buyer's country: Zid, Shopify, BigCommerce, WooCommerce, within a market on Shopify, by conversion into the customer's currency on WooCommerce (vendor choice; stated, observed: S02-VP-49|the buyer's country; S02-V-621, S02-SH-531, S02-WC-194). (e) An exchange rate held per market, set by the seller or automatic: Shopify, for markets that hold a currency (stated: S02-SH-568, S02-SH-531); a market drawn for an area within a country inherits its parent's currency (S02-SH-104, early access). Per currency: Salla, at the currency's rate (S02-SA-103; S02-SA-302 is an order field), Zid's automatic rate between two markets' currencies (S02-ZD-020), WooCommerce's manual rate (S02-WC-027)
recommendation: Engineering's: (a), (b), (c) and (e) together, with (d) as a market within a market (S02-D4). Each market may carry its own currency, inheriting the store's, and its own exchange rate, set by the seller or taken from a source, held per market rather than per currency, as Shopify holds it for markets that hold a currency (S02-SH-568); its prices are converted from the store's at that rate unless the seller sets them for the market or for a country within it. Every order, refund and report keeps its amounts in both the buyer's currency and the store's, with the market and the rate used; the store's currency stays the one for the store's own reports and the default for gift cards, a gift card in a market's currency left open (S02-E4). Sharrwah sets no payout currency: each provider pays out on its own terms (S02-R4), S02-BC-224, S02-SH-183 and S02-SH-035 being such terms. Which currencies and rate sources, and what identifies a currency in money records, are S-09's (S02-M6); a currency area within one code is S02-D9's. Rule: generality (PLAN.md section 6, step 4): one currency per store is every market inheriting it, and a rate per currency is every market of that currency taking the same rate
trade_off: Two amounts and a rate on every money record, and a rate to keep per market; in return a market can sell in its buyers' currency without touching past orders
closes: Money records that keep one currency only: an engineering cost greater than the option's value, since a second amount costs little now and a redesign later
cost_later: Split by part. Two amounts on every money record: a redesign if orders, refunds and reports keep one currency and markets later sell in their own, since every money record and report changes. The rate's level, per market or per currency: one module, a rate table. Which markets carry their own currency and prices: a setting, once both amounts are kept. D7 stands apart from S02-D6 for its first part: that later change reaches every money record, not one setting, and S-09's decision follows from it

question: A product gap: should the rules that depend on where the seller is, payment services and currency among them, be able to key on an area within a country (held as a dated field of the business record) beside the country, with a change of such an area running the checks of a move?
alternatives: (a) Not providing for it: rules key on the country only, and an area counts only where it has a country code of its own, as the references do for payment services (S02-VP-11: S02-SH-027, S02-SH-583, S02-SH-642, S02-WC-008, S02-WC-042, S02-WC-051, S02-WC-052; Shopify for a feature, S02-SH-484). (b) An area within the country as a key for some rules, as the references do for tax and one feature, stated: the tax on the platform's own fee by the seller's province (Shopify: S02-SH-513; S02-VP-15), the store's own taxes by province or state (Shopify: S02-SH-515, S02-SH-931; WooCommerce: S02-WC-118; S02-VP-16), a feature's eligibility by the province, or the part of one country, that holds the seller's fulfilment locations (Shopify: S02-SH-485, S02-SH-486; S02-VP-17). No reference keys payment services, the currency or the exchange rate on such an area, or runs a move's checks when it changes. (c) The general form: any such rule may key on the country or on an area within it, and a change of an area some rule keys on runs those rules' checks, as a move does (S02-D2)
recommendation: Engineering's, weighed against the designs read (designs.tsv): (b) now, with room kept for (c). Tax rules may key on an area, as the platforms do (S02-SH-513, S02-SH-515, S02-WC-118) and as Stripe keys a dated tax registration on a state. The area is held from the start as a dated field of its own, at two levels, the business record and the locations a store fulfils from (S-10's, S02-SH-485, S02-SH-486): a stable identifier mapped to the published subdivision code, since such codes are added, deprecated, aliased and sometimes reused (Unicode TR35); at a level named per country, since levels below the country differ between countries (OpenStreetMap); not only read from the postal address, whose area is optional and at the postal level (Google's PostalAddress). With S02-E2, extending a payment or currency rule to the area, and a move's checks to an area change, is then one module. Where the sources cut against (c): none keys payment services or currency on an area (Unicode keys a currency default on one, and calls that unusual), and Fowler finds dating a property later not hard in code, so keeping the dated area now rests on past records alone. The extension comes only from the product gap this row's evidence cites. Rule: hide what is likely to change (PLAN.md section 1), each source weighed by its kind (section 6, 'Options beyond the references')
trade_off: A dated, stable area field at two levels, used at launch by tax rules only; in return a payment or currency rule keyed on an area, or a move between areas, is one module later, and past records keep their area
closes: Nothing a reference shows. (a) as a rule of the model, countries only: an engineering cost greater than the option's value, a reading, since a dated area costs little now and past records without it can't recover it
cost_later: one module, given S02-E2's entry point and the dated area field: extending a rule to the area changes the resolver, and a move's checks on an area change change S02-D2's procedure. Fowler finds dating a property later not hard in code (designs.tsv), so what a later start can't recover is only the area on past records; whether they need it isn't shown, a reading. A redesign only where S02-E2 or S02-D1 is declined

question: A product gap: should a currency be able to name a currency area within its code, so that prices, stored amounts and reports tell two areas sharing one code apart by currency, not only by market?
alternatives: (a) Not providing for it, with one rate per currency code, as Salla, Zid and WooCommerce show (S02-SA-103, S02-ZD-020, S02-WC-027): two areas under one code sell at one rate. (b) What S02-D7, S02-E1, S02-D4 and S02-D5 already give: a market for each area, each with its own rate under the one code, each order keeping its market and rate (S02-E2); prices, stored amounts and reports then tell the areas apart only by market, and totals by currency code mix them. (c) The area named in the currency itself: a currency record (a code, and an area where one is named) that prices, amounts and reports refer to, mapped to the bare code where a provider takes only the code. No platform shows (c): Shopify's market for an area within a country inherits its parent's currency (S02-SH-104, S02-SH-072, early access)
recommendation: Engineering's, weighed against the designs read (designs.tsv): (b) now, with room kept for (c): amounts refer to a currency record, one per code at launch, which S-09 decides (S02-M6), so naming an area later is a new record, one module. The sources cut against building (c) now: the standards and platforms read identify a currency by its code alone (Unicode TR35; Java's Currency, one instance per code; Stripe's PaymentIntent, a bare ISO code), and ISO 4217's lists read the same way, a reading of its maintenance agency's page, so an area would have to map back to the bare code at every provider's boundary. They support the room's form: TigerBeetle holds each amount's currency as a number the application defines, its details kept elsewhere, and makes a changed unit a new record, not an edit. The need comes only from the product gap this row's evidence cites. Rule: hide what is likely to change (PLAN.md section 1), each source weighed by its kind (section 6, 'Options beyond the references')
trade_off: A currency table that amounts refer to, mapped to bare codes at each provider's boundary; in return a second area under one code becomes a new record, and its prices, amounts and reports can be told apart by currency
closes: Nothing a reference or a design read shows: (c) stays reachable through the currency record. What would close it is a bare code in every amount, which is S-09's to avoid (S02-M6)
cost_later: one module if amounts refer to a currency record (S-09's, S02-M6): a second area under one code is a new record with its rate; a redesign if a bare code is stored in every amount, since every money record, rate and report must then learn the area

question: How a per-market setting is read
recommendation: Engineering's: every setting that varies by market is read through one interface, and each setting declares its kind. A one-value setting (a currency, a language, a status) takes the most specific value set: the buyer's market (and a market within it), then the store's own value. A set-valued setting may combine across the markets a buyer matches: the products offered, as Shopify combines catalogs from all applicable markets (S02-SH-109); the payment methods and shipping options by engineering's own choice, a reading, since on Shopify a sub-region market customizes its own shipping (S02-SH-104). A product's restriction narrows a set, and a limit the platform or a law sets applies after values resolve and sets combine (S02-SA-283). A customer group, where a setting keys on it, is a key beside the market (S02-D4). Rule: a variation point behind one interface, bound per market (PLAN.md section 6, step 5); hide what is likely to change (section 1)
